messages.subject: covariates in spatio-temporal point process
parts:
Hi!

I am trying to build a spatio temporal point process model with INLA following the Burkitt example.
I don't have any problem if I don't need to include the covariates, however if I want to include this covariates I have problems with the stack and the dimensions.

I have seen that some time ago there was a similar questions using simulated covariates and building a raster to link the points to the mesh locations. My problem is that my covariates are already referenced to the locations (are in the original dataset), so I don't know how to proceed to include them in the stack.

Cheers,

Oscar

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] covariates in spatio-temporal point process
parts:
Hi,
To construct the point process likelihood you need the covariates not only at the observed points, but also at all the integration points for the numerical integration scheme for the integral in the likelihood. Sometimes this is on the mesh points, but sometimes not, depending on which integration scheme you use. The scheme that places integration points on the mesh nodes leads to a stable likelihood approximation, so is usually a good default choice.
  Do you have covariate values available on a grid? Is there fine scale variation in the covariates (finer than the mesh resolution)? Then you may need to use the grid as integration scheme instead, or use the grid to define the mesh points.
If the covariates are smooth, then projecting the information to the mesh nodes, or just evaluating them pointwise at the mesh nodes, can work well.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] covariates in spatio-temporal point process
parts:
For more complex lgcp models, I strongly recommend using the inlabru interface instead, since that has a helper function to setup the likelihood without the user needing to call inla.stack at all. See examples at

https://inlabru-org.github.io/inlabru/articles/

Finn
